Subject: Follow-up: Kestrel Health — buying process, security asks, and latency targets

Hi Lydia / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the decision criteria and gating items: 

Recap (from our conversation)
- Primary driver: reduce inference cost and keep inference latency below customer-facing SLAs for triage workflows.
- Target latency: p95 <= 250ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens); p95 <= 400ms for longer batch jobs called by downstream pipelines.
- Cost constraint: goal is to be in the same ballpark as current managed provider — target unit cost equivalent to <= $50 per 1M tokens (we'll refine with workloads).
- Hosting preference: Kestrel wants justification for Dedicated vs Redwood Private (VPC) — security team leans Private for PHI-sensitive flows, econ buyer prefers Dedicated if it meets SLA at lower cost.
- Procurement asks: standard MSA + PO path; procurement wants estimated lead time and invoicing cadence.
- Security asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, network diagram, data retention and key management details.

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed):
1) Action: Redwood to surface an explicit deployment recommendation (Dedicated vs Private) with expected p95 numbers and delta in unit cost (Marcus + Aditya) — target: by EOD Tuesday, 8/19.
2) Action: Share SOC 2 summary + network diagram and short KMS/HSM integration notes (attachment included).
3) Action: Procurement to confirm PO terms and whether a one-off SOW is required for Private deployment (Tom / Procurement).
4) Schedule follow-up call with Lydia (security) + Tom (procurement) + Econ buyer on Thursday 8/21 — propose 11am PT.

Attachments: SOC2_Type_II_summary.pdf (high-level), Redwood_MVP_pricing_v3.xlsx (ballpark pricing + options).

If that list looks correct, I’ll schedule the 8/21 sync and Marcus will put the deployment recommendation in writing.

Thanks,
Mina

Thanks Mina — quick clarifications from security so we can mark the ticket and share with our infosec committee: 

- SOC 2: the high-level summary is helpful; we will need the full controls mapping (control IDs mapped to evidence) prior to an executive sign-off. A redacted evidence bundle is fine for now.
- Data flow: please include an explicit statement about whether any tokenized PHI leaves our VPC in the Hosted/Dedicated flows. For Private deployment we assume no egress; confirm.
- KMS: we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) in both Dedicated and Private options and how key rotation/rotation logs are surfaced.
- SLA credits: our legal team will want example SLA language & credit calculation for downtime tied to p99 and p95 breaches.

Procurement point: Tom — can you share the internal procurement checklist so Mina knows what to prepare?

Thanks — if you can send the control mapping and a short statement on PHI egress and KMS behavior before our 8/21 sync, that will speed things up.

-Lydia
Head of InfoSec, Kestrel Health

Appreciate the detailed asks, Lydia — quick technical take from the infra side and what I’ll include in the deployment recommendation doc: 

1) PHI egress: For Hosted (standard Redwood API) tokens will traverse our control plane; we can explain the encryption-in-transit and at-rest posture, but we will recommend Dedicated or Private for any PHI-bearing workloads. For Dedicated, customer data is isolated to GPU pools and we can lock network egress with VPC peering rules. Private (customer-managed VPC) gives you full control — no control-plane egress of token payloads if you choose an on-prem/private option.

2) KMS: Both Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys via KMS. For Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS keys in supported clouds (we surface logs for key usage); for Private you can bring HSM/KMS and we can provide rotation guidance. I’ll include example rotation cadence and audit log snippets in the doc.

3) Latency expectations (p95) — ballpark numbers from our recent benchmarks (will refine using your prompt distribution):
- Dedicated (n1-standard, mid-range GPU pool): p95 ~ 180–260ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), ~300–420ms for longer prompts depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate.
- Private (on-prem equivalent): p95 comparable to Dedicated if deployed on similar GPUs; network topology matters — local VPC reduces variability.

4) Cost tradeoffs: In the recommendation I’ll show delta for three scenarios: Hosted (lowest integration effort), Dedicated (predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale), Private (highest control, upfront infra ops). I’ll include a 12-month TCO sketch using the token volumes you shared on the call.

I’ll deliver a short (1-pg) recommendation + a 1-slide cost delta table by Tuesday EOD (8/19). If that works, Mina can share it with Procurement and Security ahead of the 8/21 call.

Thanks,
Marcus
